Assertion (A): Food chains in natural ecosystems rarely comprise more than 4 or 5 trophic levels.
Reason (R): According to Lindeman's 10% law, an average of 90% of energy is lost as heat and metabolic respiration at each step, leaving an insignificant amount of usable energy after 4 trophic transfers.

Assertion (A): The concentration of non-biodegradable chemical toxins like DDT is found to be highest in top carnivores and humans.
Reason (R): Non-biodegradable chemicals cannot be broken down by cellular metabolism or excreted; they progressively bioaccumulate at each higher trophic level of a food chain.

Assertion (A): The flow of energy in an ecosystem is strictly unidirectional.
Reason (R): Solar energy captured by green plants cannot revert back to the Sun, and energy transferred to herbivores cannot flow backwards to autotrophs.

Assertion (A): The presence of the ozone layer in the stratosphere is essential for the survival of life on Earth.
Reason (R): Ozone molecules absorb damaging solar ultraviolet (UV) radiation, preventing high rates of skin cancer, cataract blindness, and genetic mutations in terrestrial organisms.

Assertion (A): Decomposer microorganisms can be completely eliminated from a forest ecosystem without altering the health of green trees.
Reason (R): Decomposers such as saprophytic bacteria and fungi break down dead organic matter and plant litter, recycling essential mineral nutrients back into the soil for root absorption.

Assertion (A): Agricultural crop fields and botanical gardens are designated as artificial (man-made) ecosystems.
Reason (R): They are planned, planted, and artificially regulated by humans through plowing, weeding, fertilizing, and irrigation rather than evolving naturally.

Assertion (A): The use of disposable paper cups is environmentally superior to disposable plastic cups for serving beverages on passenger trains.
Reason (R): Paper is an organic biodegradable material composed of plant cellulose that is decomposed by natural soil bacteria without leaving toxic persistent residues.

Assertion (A): Terrestrial green plants capture about 10% of the total solar energy that strikes the surface of their leaves.
Reason (R): Photosynthetic pigments in green plant leaves capture only about 1% of incident sunlight energy and convert it into chemical bond energy in carbohydrates.

Assertion (A): Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) cause widespread destruction of the stratospheric ozone layer.
Reason (R): When struck by high-energy solar UV photons, CFC molecules release free chlorine atoms (Cl radicals) that catalytically convert ozone (O3) into ordinary oxygen (O2) in repeating chain reactions.

Assertion (A): A given agricultural area of cropland can sustain a substantially larger human population if people consume a plant-based diet rather than a meat-based diet.
Reason (R): Consuming crops directly places humans at the second trophic level, bypassing the 90% energy loss incurred when feeding crops to intermediate livestock.
